recipes.title: Gulyás (Hungarian Beef Goulash Soup)
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of Hungarian beef goulash soup with tender beef, potatoes, carrots, and peppers in a deep paprika-red broth
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Goulash Simmering in a Traditional Bogrács Cauldron
recipes.prep_alt: Beef goulash simmering over an open fire in a traditional Hungarian bogrács cauldron, stirred with a long wooden spoon

sections.heading: Steps
items: Ask an adult to help heat the oil or lard in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef cubes in batches, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion and garlic until soft.
Take the pot off the heat for a moment and stir in the paprika, caraway, and marjoram so the paprika doesn't scorch.
Return the beef to the pot, then add the tomato paste, diced tomatoes, bay leaf, and stock or water.
Cover and simmer 60–75 minutes, until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the potatoes, carrot, and green pepper, and simmer 20 minutes more, until the vegetables are tender and the beef is fully tender.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve hot, with crusty bread.

recipes.title: Chicken Paprikash with Nokedli (Csirkepaprikás)
recipes.dish_alt: Bone-in chicken thighs in a silky red paprika and sour cream sauce, served over soft nokedli egg dumplings
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Paprika Chicken Simmering in Its Sauce
recipes.prep_alt: Chicken paprikash simmering in a creamy red paprika sauce with a dollop of sour cream, before being ladled over the nokedli

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: All-purpose flour, to thicken the sour cream

sections.heading: Steps
items: Ask an adult to help heat the lard or oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken thighs skin-side down, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the onion and garlic until soft.
Take the pot off the heat for a moment and stir in the paprika so it blooms without burning.
Add the green pepper, tomato, and chicken stock, then return the chicken to the pot.
Cover and simmer 30–35 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Meanwhile, make the nokedli: whisk the nokedli flour, egg, water, and salt into a thick, sticky batter. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Drop small spoonfuls of the batter into the boiling water (or push through a colander) and cook 2–3 minutes, until they float. Drain.
Remove the chicken from the sauce. Whisk the flour into the sour cream until smooth, then stir it into the sauce and simmer gently 2 minutes to thicken (don't let it boil hard).
Return the chicken to the sauce, and season with salt and pepper.
Serve the chicken and sauce hot over the nokedli.

recipes.title: Töltött Káposzta (Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
recipes.dish_alt: Two Hungarian stuffed cabbage rolls simmered in a paprika-red tomato sauce, served in a floral-rimmed bowl
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Cabbage Rolls on a Bed of Sauerkraut, with Sour Cream
recipes.prep_alt: Sliced stuffed cabbage rolls plated with sauerkraut and a dollop of sour cream on the side

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Smoked sausage (kolbász) or smoked bacon, sliced

sections.heading: Steps
items: In a bowl, mix the ground pork, rice, egg, onion, garlic, paprika, caraway, salt, and pepper.
Lay a cabbage leaf flat, spoon some filling near the base, fold in the sides, and roll up snugly. Repeat with the remaining leaves.
Spread half the sauerkraut over the bottom of a heavy pot.
Arrange the cabbage rolls seam-side down on top and scatter the smoked sausage or bacon around them.
Cover with the remaining sauerkraut, then add the bay leaf and the water or stock.
Bring to a boil, then cover, reduce the heat, and simmer 60 minutes, until the rolls are cooked through and the cabbage is tender.
Serve hot with a generous dollop of sour cream.

recipes.title: Lecsó with Sausage and Egg
recipes.dish_alt: A small pot of Hungarian lecsó stew with peppers, tomatoes, smoked sausage, and a poached egg on top
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Egg Scrambled Through the Peppers and Tomatoes
recipes.prep_alt: Lecsó with beaten egg scrambled through the stewed peppers, onion, and tomato just before serving

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Banana peppers or sweet frying peppers, sliced

sections.heading: Steps
items: Ask an adult to help heat the oil or lard in a pan and sauté the onion until soft.
Take the pan off the heat for a moment and stir in the paprika.
Add the peppers and cook 5 minutes, until starting to soften.
Add the tomatoes and sausage, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, until the peppers are tender and everything is saucy.
Season with salt and pepper.
Push everything to one side of the pan, pour in the beaten egg, and scramble gently until just set, then stir it through the rest of the lecsó.
Serve hot with bread.

recipes.title: Hortobágyi Palacsinta (Savory Meat-Filled Crêpes)
recipes.dish_alt: A savory Hortobágyi palacsinta crêpe roll filled with shredded paprika chicken, plated in a pool of sour cream sauce
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Filled Crêpe Rolls Before Baking Under the Sauce
recipes.prep_alt: Two savory crêpe rolls filled with paprika chicken, plated and covered in paprika sour cream sauce

sections.heading: Crêpe Batter
rows: Oil or butter, for frying crêpes

sections.heading: Sauce
rows: Sweet Hungarian paprika, for the sauce

sections.heading: Steps
items: Make the crêpe batter: whisk the flour, egg, milk, and salt together until smooth. Let rest 10 minutes.
Heat a little oil or butter in a nonstick pan and cook thin crêpes, one at a time, until lightly golden on both sides. Stack them and set aside.
For the filling, heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion and garlic until soft.
Take the pot off the heat for a moment and stir in the paprika and caraway.
Add the chicken, tomato, and chicken stock. Cover and simmer 20–25 minutes, until the chicken is very tender, then shred it with two forks right in the sauce.
Season the filling with salt and pepper. Spoon some filling onto each crêpe, roll it up, and arrange the rolls seam-side down in a baking dish.
For the sauce, whisk the flour into the sour cream until smooth, then stir in a few tablespoons of the hot liquid left in the filling pot along with the paprika for the sauce, until pourable.
Pour the sauce evenly over the crêpes.
Warm through, covered, over low heat or in a low oven for about 10 minutes, until hot and bubbling at the edges.
Serve hot.

recipes.title: Székely Gulyás (Pork and Sauerkraut Stew)
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of Székely gulyás — creamy pork and sauerkraut stew topped with sour cream, tomato, and olives
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Pork and Sauerkraut Simmering in the Paprika Sauce
recipes.prep_alt: Pork chunks and sauerkraut simmering in a creamy paprika sauce, close up in a white bowl

sections.heading: Steps
items: Ask an adult to help heat the oil or lard in a pot and sauté the onion until soft.
Add the pork and brown it on all sides.
Take the pot off the heat for a moment and stir in the paprika and caraway (adding them off the heat, with a splash of the water or stock, keeps the paprika from burning). Stir in the garlic.
Cover and simmer 40 minutes, adding a little more water or stock if it looks dry, until the pork is nearly tender.
Stir in the sauerkraut, bay leaf, and the remaining water or stock.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes more, until the pork and sauerkraut are both tender.
Stir in the sour cream and season with salt and pepper. Warm through gently without letting it boil hard.
Serve hot with bread.

recipes.title: Rakott Krumpli (Layered Potato, Egg & Sausage Bake)
recipes.dish_alt: A serving of rakott krumpli — layered potato, egg, and sausage bake topped with sour cream and paprika
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Fresh from the Oven, Golden and Bubbling
recipes.prep_alt: The whole rakott krumpli casserole fresh out of the oven in its baking dish, golden and bubbling on top

sections.heading: Steps
items: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Grease a baking dish with the butter.
Layer a third of the sliced potatoes in the bottom of the dish and season with salt and pepper.
Top with half the sliced egg and half the sausage, then dollop over a third of the sour cream.
Repeat the layers once more, then finish with a top layer of potatoes and the last of the sour cream spread evenly over the top.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake 30–35 minutes, until bubbling and lightly golden on top.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving hot.

recipes.title: Somlói Galuska (Bonus — Hungarian Trifle Sponge Dessert)
recipes.dish_alt: A glass of Somlói galuska showing layers of cocoa and walnut sponge cake, custard, whipped cream, and chocolate drizzle
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Layered with Whipped Cream and Chopped Walnuts
recipes.prep_alt: Somlói galuska assembled in a cup with sponge cubes, custard, whipped cream, and a scatter of chopped walnuts on top

sections.heading: Sponge Cake
rows: Cocoa powder, for half the batter
Walnuts, chopped, for half the batter

sections.heading: Steps
items: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a small baking pan.
Whisk the egg and sugar together until pale, then fold in the flour and baking powder to make a smooth batter.
Split the batter in half. Stir the cocoa powder into one half and the chopped walnuts (for the batter) into the other half.
Spread each half into the pan side by side, keeping them separate, and bake 12–15 minutes, until springy to the touch. Let cool, then cut into cubes.
Meanwhile, make the rum syrup: warm the water and sugar together until the sugar dissolves, remove from the heat, and stir in the rum. Soak the raisins in a splash of the warm syrup.
Make the custard: whisk the egg yolk, sugar, and cornstarch together, then whisk in the milk. Return to low heat and stir constantly until thickened. Stir in the vanilla and let cool.
To assemble, layer the cocoa and walnut sponge cubes in a glass or dish, brushing each layer generously with the rum syrup and scattering over the soaked raisins.
Spoon the vanilla custard over the top.
Finish with the whipped cream, a drizzle of melted chocolate, and a scattering of the walnuts for topping.
Chill briefly, then serve.
